object_description: elongated school wing and perpendicular gymnasium around a courtyard
design_condition: The elongated wing on the northern edge and the perpendicular gymnasium form a courtyard-like playground, while the western park connects the complex to the district and the eastern playing field requires substantial earthworks.

positive.statement: The precise placement of the new buildings creates a clear situation with two strong outdoor spaces.

position.rationale: Perpendicular wing and gymnasium visibly define two distinct outdoor spaces around the courtyard.

positive.statement: The landscape concept creates a natural embedding, a clear address and diverse open spaces with high atmospheric and functional quality.

position.rationale: Western park, courtyard, and eastern field are visible as differentiated exterior zones.

positive.statement: The moderate height development and striking longitudinal section are appropriate and harmonious for a primary school.

position.rationale: Moderate-height wing and contrasting longitudinal section are clearly visible across the model views.

positive.statement: The internal structure of the elongated building is simple and clear.

position.rationale: The long northern wing is directly legible in the top and elevation projections.

positive.statement: The first floor forms a memorable learning landscape with three clusters and well-lit classrooms.

position.rationale: The first-floor band is visible, while clusters and classroom interiors require an approximate anchor.

positive.statement: The clearly structured areas with their own entrances convey a feeling of home and enable autonomous use.

position.rationale: Separate entrances are approximated along the long wing’s southern frontage without distinct markers.

positive.statement: The construction system should enable efficient and sustainable construction through a clear grid and robust details.

position.rationale: Regular longitudinal massing and repeated elevation bands provide direct evidence for a clear structural system.

negative.statement: A different solution would have to be found for the grass playing field because of the difficult earthworks and embankment situation.

position.rationale: The eastern open field is visible beside the gymnasium, though embankment geometry is only partially represented.

negative.statement: The arrangement of group rooms in the existing building is unsuitable.

position.rationale: Existing group rooms are not distinguishable; the anchor approximates the western portion of the wing.

negative.statement: The care-area intersections with the staircases are not ideal.

position.rationale: Care and stair intersections are internal and approximated within the central wing.

negative.statement: The large room depths on the ground and basement floors create inadequate lighting conditions.

position.rationale: Ground and basement levels are constrained by the lower elevation bands of the elongated wing.

negative.statement: The determining facade material is viewed critically with regard to the resulting expression.

position.rationale: Facade surfaces are clearly visible in elevations, but sampled points do not identify material.

negative.statement: The stepped section reduces the available space and the efficiency of the photovoltaic system.

position.rationale: The stepped longitudinal profile is directly visible toward the eastern end of the wing.

negative.statement: The high spatial quality is limited to the well-lit clusters on the top floor, while lower rooms are less flexible and difficult to use in terms of lighting.

position.target: well-lit clusters on the top floor
position.rationale: Top-floor bands are visible, but lighting quality and cluster interiors are not directly represented.
